input.question: Does eating dirt as a child have any proven benefits for your immune system?
input.ground_truth: Not so much a boosted immune system, but polio affected the upper and middle class far worse than the lower class because kids were exposed to the virus early on in low income areas. As a consequence they became immune to it, while the upper class kids were exposed later in life when it had a far more deleterious effect. [source](_URL_0_)

Okay, let’s imagine your body is like a garden. Eating dirt is like putting a bunch of random stuff from the ground into your garden. Some people think that this might help your body learn how to fight germs better, kind of like how getting a little bit of dirt can help your garden grow stronger plants.

But, scientists have looked into this a lot, and they haven’t found any real proof that eating dirt is good for your immune system (that’s the part of your body that helps you fight off sickness). In fact, eating dirt can be dangerous because it might have things in it that can make you sick, like tiny bugs or chemicals.

So, even though playing in the dirt outside can help you get used to different germs (which might help your immune system a little bit), **eating** dirt is not a good idea. It’s better to wash your hands and eat clean, healthy food!
